prompt:
Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Several prominent open-source projects, most notably **curl** and **Python**, have publicly documented the burden of AI-generated low-quality submissions, often referred to as "AI slop." Below are the documented examples with the required citation format.

### Curl (Daniel Stenberg)

The curl project has been the most vocal about this issue, culminating in the termination of its bug bounty program in early 2026 due to the volume of invalid AI-generated reports.

SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/01/overrun-with-ai-slop-curl-scraps-bounties-to-ensure-intact-mental-health/ | QUOTE: "We are just a small single open source project with a small number of active maintainers," Daniel Stenberg, the founder and lead developer of the open source app cURL, said Thursday. "It is not in our power to change how all these people and their slop machines work. We need to make moves to ensure our survival and intact mental health." | CLAIM: Curl scrapped its vulnerability reward program because the volume of AI-generated "slop" was threatening the mental health and survival of the small maintainer team.

SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/01/overrun-with-ai-slop-curl-scraps-bounties-to-ensure-intact-mental-health/ | QUOTE: "We will ban you and ridicule you in public if you waste our time on crap reports." | CLAIM: Daniel Stenberg issued a public warning that submitters of low-quality AI reports would face bans and public ridicule.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "That's it. I've had it. I'm putting my foot down on this craziness." | CLAIM: In May 2025, Daniel Stenberg announced new screening measures for HackerOne submissions after reaching his limit with AI-generated reports.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "We now ban every reporter instantly who submits reports we deem AI slop," Stenberg added. "A threshold has been reached. We are effectively being DDoSed. If we could, we would charge them for this waste of our time." | CLAIM: Stenberg described the influx of AI reports as akin to a DDoS attack and instituted an instant ban policy for such submissions.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "I personally spend an insane amount of time on curl already, wasting three hours still leaves time for other things. My fellows however are not full time on curl. They might only have three hours per week for curl. Not to mention the emotional toll it takes to deal with these mind-numbing stupidities." | CLAIM: Stenberg highlighted the disproportionate time burden and emotional toll AI reports placed on volunteer maintainers who have limited weekly availability.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "because getting a lot of security reports I mean first they get longer and more they have more contents these days right they sort of get worse but they also get longer and more complicated... because that’s what AI does. is not only the volume goes up, the quality goes down. So we spend more time than ever to get less out of it than ever." | CLAIM: Stenberg explained that AI generates reports that are simultaneously lower in quality and higher in volume/complexity, resulting in a net negative efficiency for maintainers.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "It is a little bit of abuse because most of these, that we call them AI slop, they’re just generated by someone really quickly. They don’t really understand it, they haven’t really verified it. The AI told them this is a problem, they pass it on to us. No effort, quick, easy for them and we get a couple of hours of work per every such instance. It doesn’t work." | CLAIM: Stenberg characterized the submission of unverified AI outputs as a form of abuse that shifts hours of verification work from the submitter to the maintainer.

### Python (Seth Larson)

The Python project also raised concerns about the resource drain caused by these reports.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports," Larson wrote. | CLAIM: Seth Larson from the Python project noted that time-wasting security reports cause significant psychological stress and isolation for maintainers.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "All of these feelings can add to burnout of likely highly trusted contributors to open source projects." | CLAIM: Larson warned that the accumulation of stress from bogus reports contributes to contributor burnout.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "In many ways, these low-quality reports should be treated as if they are malicious. Even if this is not their intent, the outcome is maintainers that are burnt out and more averse to legitimate security work." | CLAIM: Larson argued that low-quality AI reports should be treated as malicious acts because their outcome is the same: burnt-out maintainers.

### Other Projects (FFmpeg)

Daniel Stenberg also referenced discussions with other projects facing similar overload issues.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/videos/daniel-stenberg-ai-onslop/ | QUOTE: "We heard about this other project sort of I talked to the FFMPEG people and when they sure they get a lot of valid reports from one of these tech giants and just overload them with a lot of that’s also work. So you need to handle that somehow." | CLAIM: Stenberg cited conversations with FFmpeg maintainers who were being overloaded by a high volume of reports, including valid ones, from large tech entities, illustrating a broader industry burden.
